text: Swimming is a high-energy sport that allows athletes to glide effortlessly through water while covering great distances in a short amount of time. One of the fundamental components of swimming is laps, which provide a structured way to measure performance and improve speed. By swimming laps continuously, swimmers can learn to build endurance and practice their technique under controlled conditions. The number of laps completed in a set time frame, often measured in meters or kilometers, is a popular objective for competitive swimmers and fitness enthusiasts alike. Alongside laps, swimming also involves the use of goggles, essential for protecting the eyes while underwater, and enhancing the swimmer's ability to see clearly while executing their strokes and turns.
